datasets.name: Morphology of human corneal endothelium in situ.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)
datasets.role: Homo sapiens, corneal endothelium (alizarin red, in situ)

method: Cells in each image were segmented with Cellpose CPSAM v2 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform (claim-sources/cell-geometry/segment.py; operation IDs and model checksum in claim-sources/cell-geometry/results/<image>/cellpose.json). claim-sources/cell-geometry/analyze.py closes inter-cell gaps, finds points where three or more cells meet, estimates each wall's direction from wall pixels 0.08-0.25 median cell diameters from the junction, counts neighbours of cells fully surrounded by segmented cells, and runs the same measurement on three synthetic tilings (hexagonal lattice, brick wall, random Voronoi) as calibration.
hypothesis: If tissue cell walls meet three at a time at 120 degrees regardless of cell size, junction angles in real tissues cluster near 120 degrees more tightly than in a random partition of the plane, T-shaped junctions are rare, four cells do not meet at one point, and angle deviation does not depend on cell size.
pass_criterion: Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test. A tissue conforms if its junction-angle SD and its fraction of T-like junctions (largest angle >= 160 deg) are both below the random-Voronoi control. Supports if every usable tissue conforms; mixed if some do and some do not; refutes if none do.
fail_criterion: Refutes if no tissue has both an angle SD and a T-junction fraction below the random-Voronoi control.

test_contract.expected_observation: In planar sections of a cellular tissue, the three angles at each three-way wall junction cluster near 120 degrees: junction-angle SD and T-junction fraction are both below those of a random Voronoi tiling of the same cell count.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Junction angles in a tissue are as dispersed as, or more dispersed than, a random Voronoi tiling, or T-junctions (one angle near 180 degrees) are the majority, as in cell-file tissues such as grass epidermis.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public micrographs of planar (one-cell-thick or surface) tissue with resolvable cell walls, segmentable to label images; not drawings or diagrams; not images used to illustrate the claim in the source; licence permitting reuse. Segmenter output must be calibrated against synthetic tilings with known junction statistics (see revisions).
test_contract.inference_method: Cellpose-SAM segmentation, three-way junction extraction from the label image, angle SD and T-junction fraction per tissue, compared with a perfect hexagonal lattice and a random Voronoi control; pass if both statistics fall below the random control, with segmenter bias measured on synthetic tilings and subtracted from the margin.

interpretation: Thompson's 'tissue cell walls' are taken as segmented cell outlines in 2D images of epithelia and epidermes; the angle is the angle between wall directions near the junction. The compound eye is included as a packing of ommatidia, not of single cells.

measured.unit: tissues (of those usable) whose junction-angle SD and T-junction fraction are both below the random-Voronoi control, as measured on Cellpose-SAM output (see revisions for segmenter bias)

not_used.arabidopsis-shoot-section: crop missed the intended panel; segmentation unusable

caveats: Segmenter bias (added 2026-10-31 after external review): Cellpose-SAM pulls non-hexagonal packings toward 120-degree junctions (brick wall 100% -> 3-16% T-junctions). Conforming tissues are consistent with 120-degree packing but their margin over the random control is inflated; see revisions[0].

Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test.
One image per tissue, all from Wikimedia Commons; tissues were chosen by availability, not sampled.
Four-way junction fractions are upper bounds: the random-Voronoi control, which has no true four-way vertices, scores 8.6% because close three-way junctions merge.
Weak negative size-deviation correlations in some tissues also appear in the random control, so they are attributed to measurement noise in small cells.
The Drosophila eye image is an SEM of a curved surface; projection distorts its angles.

to.summary: 4 of 5 tissues are not cell-file tissues; margin over the random control is inflated by the segmenter

revisions.reason: Segmenter-bias null (claim-sources/cell-geometry/segmenter_bias.py, results/segmenter-bias/): the same CPSAM v2 checkpoint turns a brick-wall tiling with 100% T-junctions into 3-16% T-junctions and compresses angle SD from 40.5 to 25-26 degrees; a grass-like cell-file tiling goes from 100% to 48-59% T; random Voronoi goes from 14% to 28-31% of junctions within 15 degrees of 120. Cell counts were exact, so the bias is in boundary shape. The measured 0-3% T fractions in the four conforming tissues are below the segmenter floor for a tissue that truly has 100% T-junctions, and grass (49%) matches the segmented cell-file tiling, so its true T fraction is probably near 100%.
